subject: Coefficients of the C matrix of a extended mesh

messages.author: 8dbb28b015bb7762
messages.subject: Coefficients of the C matrix of a extended mesh
parts:
Hi list!

I was having some odd results when using an extended mesh (in order to
avoid the border effect) in a spde model. I finally tracked the problem
down to the C matrix element of the spde object.
I expected something that does not hold, and I don't understand why.

According to the 'going off grid' paper, the diagonal elements of the C
matrix represent the 'volumes' of the dual mesh, for each of the
vertices. But when I use an extended mesh, these values (for the
vertices in the non-extended region) are different from those of a
regular mesh, while I expected them to be the same.

Please see the clarifying code below.
Thanks in advance .
ï¿½acu.-

### Question about the spde C matrix ###
require(INLA)
loc.bnd = matrix(c(0,0, 1,0, 1,1, 0,1), 4, 2, byrow=TRUE)
segm.bnd = inla.mesh.segment(loc.bnd)

# create a regular and a extended mesh and the corresponding spdes
mesh = inla.mesh.create(loc=NULL,
boundary=segm.bnd,
refine=list(max.edge=0.1))
spde = inla.spde.create(mesh, model="matern")

mesh2 <- inla.mesh.create.helper(points=NULL, points.domain=loc,
boundary=list(inla.mesh.segment(cbind(loc.bnd, 0.0), is.bnd=TRUE), NULL),
offset=c(1, 20)*0.1,
max.edge=c(1, 10)*0.1)
spde2 = inla.spde.create(mesh2, model="matern")

# within the unit square, the meshes are (almost) the same
plot(mesh)
dev.new(); plot.new()
plot(mesh2, add=T)

# identify which points of the extended mesh lie within the square
int.idx <- point.in.polygon(mesh2$loc[,1], mesh2$loc[,2],
mesh2$loc[mesh2$segm$int$idx[,1],1], mesh2$loc[mesh2$segm$int$idx[,1],2])
int.idx <- int.idx != 0 # select interior or boundary points of the polygon

# they are exactly the first mesh$n points
all.equal(1:mesh$n, which(int.idx))

# and the vertices are exactly the same
plot(mesh)
points(mesh2$loc[int.idx, ], col='red', pch=20)

# but the (diagonal) C matrices...
iw = diag(spde$internal$c0)
iw2 = diag(spde2$internal$c0)

# ... have very different coefficients in the diagonal
plot(iw, iw2[int.idx], pch=20)
abline(c(0,1))
#########################################

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: Coefficients of the C matrix of a extended mesh
parts:
On Thursday, 15 March 2012 14:35:38 UTC+1, Facundo Muñoz wrote:

all.equal(1:mesh$n, which(int.idx))
# they are exactly the first mesh$n points
# and the vertices are exactly the same

Here you implicitly made the assumption that the points are in the same _order_ in both meshes.  They are not.

The way the triangulation algorithm works is not always easily predictable.  One might think that a regular set of input points would produce a predictable output, but due to robustness considerations, points are added in different order depending on whether they are known to blong to a boundary or not.

The following comparison shows that most of the points do have the same C-diagonal values (the exception being the points on the boundary of the regular interior):

plot(1:mesh$n, sort(iw), pch=20, xlim=c(-300,300), ylim=c(0,0.01))
points(-(1:mesh$n), sort(iw2[int.idx]), col='red', pch=20)

If you want more control over a regular interior, specify a lattice (see inla.mesh.lattice) and use $idx$loc to map between your input order and the resulting order in the mesh.  Note that when a regular lattice is extended, the triangulation will not necessarily be regular in the interior, since the irregular behaviour in the extension can "creep" into the interior.  This mostly happens when max.edge is set to a value smaller than the input lattice resolution.

/Finn
